methodology: Each opportunity was collected from the issuing organization's public page. The source URL is the page used at collection time; the opportunity URL is the official call or program page. Deadlines and amounts are copied from those pages, not inferred.

items.title: 2027 ACGME Annual Educational Conference — Call for Abstracts
items.organization: Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education
items.description: The ACGME invites in-person poster abstracts for the 2027 Annual Educational Conference. Submissions should address accreditation and management of GME programs and Sponsoring Institutions, for DIOs, program directors, coordinators, residents, fellows, faculty, and hospital administrators. Abstracts require background, objectives, methods, results/outcomes, and significance beyond the local setting.
items.deadlineNote: 5:00 p.m. Central

items.title: Learn Serve Lead 2027 — Call for Medical Education Submissions
items.description: AAMC is accepting medical education submissions for Learn Serve Lead 2027 in three types: Sessions on Medical Education; Medical Education Innovation Abstracts; and Medical Education Research Abstracts. The meeting convenes medical schools and teaching hospitals across campuses, disciplines, and missions.

items.title: IAMSE 2027 — Poster and Oral Abstract Submissions
items.organization: International Association of Medical Science Educators
items.description: Call for poster and oral abstracts for the 31st Annual IAMSE Conference, themed “Stronger Together: From Myths to Evidence in the Evolving Landscape of Health Science Education.” Author notifications are expected in March 2027.
items.deadlineNote: 11:59 p.m. EDT

items.title: IAMSE 2027 — Focus Session Abstracts
items.organization: International Association of Medical Science Educators
items.description: 90-minute Focus Sessions for small-group interactive discussion. No more than one-third of the time may be lecture. Multi-institutional and interprofessional submissions are encouraged. Deadline was 1 September 2026.
items.deadlineNote: 11:59 p.m. EDT

items.title: APMEC 2027 — Asia Pacific Medical Education Conference
items.description: Workshop/symposium/panel proposals were due 15 April 2026; oral presentation abstracts were due 3 June 2026. The conference itself remains a major Asia-Pacific gathering for health professions educators.

items.title: AMEE Conference 2027 — Helsinki
items.organization: AMEE – The International Association for Health Professions Education
items.description: AMEE’s 2027 annual conference will be held in Helsinki, Finland, 28 August – 1 September 2027, including the Integrated Ottawa Event. Full registration and abstract-call details are still being posted by AMEE.

items.title: ICRE 2026 — International Conference on Residency Education
items.organization: Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada
items.description: World’s largest conference devoted to residency education. 2026 theme: “Thriving in Uncertainty: Residency Education in a World of Change.” Abstract submissions closed 14 January 2026. Early-bird registration has been advertised.

items.title: ICRE 2027 — Halifax
items.organization: Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada
items.description: ICRE returns to Halifax, Nova Scotia, 28–30 October 2027. The call for abstracts has not yet been posted on the conference site.

items.title: Learn Serve Lead 2026 — AAMC Annual Meeting
items.description: AAMC’s 150th anniversary annual meeting in Anaheim. Registration is open. Medical education scholarship submissions for this meeting have closed; the 2027 call is now the active submission cycle.

items.title: 2027 Emerging Technologies for Teaching and Learning
items.description: Conference on creative approaches, emerging technologies, and innovative teaching practices across the health professions. Digital demonstrations call closed 14 August 2026.

items.title: SoTL Commons Conference 2027
items.description: Scholarship of Teaching and Learning commons conference. Call opens August 2026 with a 23 October 2026 deadline, per the University of Saskatchewan MedEd conference listing compiled from organizer pages.
items.sourceName: University of Saskatchewan MedEd conference listings

items.title: STFM Annual Spring Conference 2027
items.organization: Society of Teachers of Family Medicine
items.description: STFM’s annual spring meeting for family medicine educators. Abstract deadline not yet posted on the compiled 2027 listing.
items.sourceName: University of Saskatchewan MedEd conference listings

items.title: SACME Annual Meeting 2027
items.organization: Society for Academic Continuing Medical Education
items.description: Annual meeting of continuing medical education scholars and leaders. Abstract deadline listed as TBA.
items.sourceName: University of Saskatchewan MedEd conference listings

items.title: Family Medicine Forum 2026
items.organization: College of Family Physicians of Canada
items.description: Canada’s national family medicine conference. Abstract deadline for 2026 is closed.
items.sourceName: University of Saskatchewan MedEd conference listings

items.title: ISSOTL 2026 Conference
items.organization: International Society for the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning
items.description: International SoTL conference, relevant to medical and health professions educators working on teaching scholarship.
items.sourceName: University of Saskatchewan MedEd conference listings

items.title: AAMC GEA National Grant Award
items.organization: Association of American Medical Colleges — Group on Educational Affairs
items.description: Funds medical education research on problems such as professional identity formation, learner well-being and mistreatment, the learning environment, faculty development, interprofessional education, competency-based education, EPAs and milestones, self-regulated learning, and virtual learning. Multiple two-year awards of up to USD 10,000. Pre-proposals open in the fall; invited full proposals follow in the spring. AAMC currently lists this call as closed.
items.deadlineNote: Annual two-step call: pre-proposal in the fall, full proposal in the spring. Watch the GEA grants page for the next opening.
items.amount: Up to USD 10,000 (two years; multiple awards)
items.eligibility: Faculty at LCME- or CACMS-accredited schools or COTH member hospitals in the USA or Canada; medical students, residents, and fellows may be co-investigators
items.sourceName: AAMC GEA grants for medical educators

items.title: AAMC NEXT Grant (Nurturing Experiences for Tomorrow’s Community Leaders)
items.description: Institutional funding to develop or enhance a learning opportunity for medical students, residents, and other interprofessional learners that improves community health and reduces health disparities with community partners. The public page currently lists 2023–2025 grantees and does not post a new application window.
items.deadlineNote: No open cycle is posted. Contact AAMC (kcarkuff@aamc.org) or watch the NEXT Grant page.
items.eligibility: AAMC-member accredited medical schools, teaching hospitals, and ACGME-accredited U.S. residency programs (per prior cycle)

items.title: AMA ChangeMedEd Innovation Grant Program
items.description: One-year grants for novel experiments in undergraduate medical education, GME, or practice, with a community of practice inside the AMA ChangeMedEd Consortium. Inter-institutional collaborations are especially competitive. The 2025–2026 cohort focused on competency-based medical education and intersections with AI assessment, educational equity, coaching, master adaptive learners, health systems science assessment, and sharing competency data. Recipients are posted; the next application window is not yet listed.
items.deadlineNote: Recurring ChangeMedEd cycle. Watch the Innovation Grants page for the next call.
items.eligibility: Medical educators across UME, GME, and practice; minimum of two investigators including the PI

items.title: AMA ChangeMedEd Bright Ideas Showcase Grant
items.description: At ChangeMedEd 2025, attendees selected three Bright Ideas that use AI to transform medical education. Each received a USD 20,000 grant and joined a one-year community of practice with the 2025 Innovation Grant recipients. Recipients include Creighton (Phoenix), UNC Chapel Hill, and the University of Michigan. Watch ChangeMedEd for a future showcase.
items.deadlineNote: Tied to the ChangeMedEd conference showcase. The 2025 awards have been made.
items.eligibility: Ideas presented at the ChangeMedEd Bright Ideas Showcase

items.title: AMA Transforming Lifelong Learning Through Precision Education Grant Program
items.description: Four-year institutional grants to build precision-education systems that use data and AI to tailor learning for medical students, residents, and practicing physicians. Letters of intent were due 21 April 2025; 11 teams (more than 80 institutions) were announced on 13 January 2026, each receiving USD 1.1 million over four years. The program is a USD 12 million AMA investment through ChangeMedEd.
items.deadlineNote: Letter of intent; invited full proposals followed. Recipients announced 13 January 2026.
items.amount: USD 1.1 million over four years (11 teams; USD 12 million program)
items.eligibility: Single or partnering U.S.-based institutions across medical school, residency, and continuing education

items.title: Joan F. Giambalvo Fund for the Advancement of Women
items.organization: American Medical Association Women Physicians Section and AMA Foundation
items.description: Research awards of up to USD 10,000 on professional issues affecting women physicians and medical students, including leadership, practice patterns, satisfaction and burnout, retention, and practice re-entry. The AMA page (updated 25 September 2025) lists the 2025 recipient and does not yet post a 2026 deadline.
items.deadlineNote: Annual research award. Watch the Giambalvo Fund page for the next application window.
items.eligibility: Principal or co-principal investigator must be a physician (MD/DO) or a U.S. LCME- or COCA-accredited medical student

items.title: AMEE Research Grant
items.organization: AMEE – The International Association for Health Professions Education
items.description: Annual two-step research grant for health professions education projects by AMEE individual members (not student members). Up to £10,000 for costs such as simulated-patient fees, participant incentives, transcription, research-assistant salary, and research-group meetings — not core-team salary, equipment, travel (except group meetings), or overhead. The 2026 cycle closed; Dr Van Nguyen was named the 2026 recipient on 19 August 2026. Grantees must present at AMEE 2026 or 2027.
items.deadlineNote: Pre-proposals due 16 January 2026; invited full proposals due 31 May 2026. The 2026 cycle is closed.
items.eligibility: AMEE individual members (PI or an associate investigator); not available to student members

items.title: AMEE Faculty Development Research Grant
items.organization: AMEE – The International Association for Health Professions Education
items.description: One project of up to £7,000 for faculty-development research only; other topics are declined. Open to paid AMEE individual members (PI or an associate investigator). The 2026 cycle closed; Lianne Loosveld (Maastricht University), with Eline Vanassche and Diana Dolmans, was named the 2026 recipient on 23 July 2026. Presentation at AMEE 2026 or 2027 is required.
items.deadlineNote: Pre-proposals due 16 January 2026; invited full proposals due 15 May 2026. The 2026 cycle is closed.
items.eligibility: AMEE individual members (PI or an associate investigator); not available to students; faculty-development topics only

items.title: AMEE MERCS Grant (Medical Educators in Resource-Constrained Settings)
items.organization: AMEE – The International Association for Health Professions Education
items.description: Two grants of up to £2,000 for health professions education research in economies in transition or developing economies, including settings affected by conflict, migration, poverty, or limited health services. Includes a one-year resource-constrained AMEE membership, AMEE Guides access, and optional research mentorship. AMEE membership is not required. Students are excluded. The 2026 cycle closed 10 April 2026; winners announced 15 July 2026 (Sri Lanka and Pakistan projects).
items.deadlineNote: The 2026 cycle is closed. Watch the MERCS Grant page for the next round.
items.amount: Up to £2,000 (two awards) plus one-year AMEE membership
items.eligibility: Teams (not students) at institutions in developing economies or economies in transition; AMEE membership not required

items.title: AMEE–ScholarRx Grant
items.organization: AMEE – The International Association for Health Professions Education (with ScholarRx)
items.description: Supports development, implementation, and evaluation of innovative, shareable health professions curricula as multiple Rx Bricks on the ScholarRx platform, later posted on AMEE and ScholarRx sites. The winning team receives up to £4,000, Rx Bricks Create access, training, 200 one-year student subscriptions, and AMEE dissemination. The 2026 call is closed (initial applications were due 27 March 2026; invited full proposals 9 August 2026; awards 31 August 2026).
items.deadlineNote: Initial applications due 27 March 2026; invited full proposals due 9 August 2026. AMEE lists the 2026 call as closed.
items.amount: Up to £4,000 plus platform access, training, and 200 student subscriptions
items.eligibility: Teams in any health profession; all members must be current AMEE members; student-only teams are not eligible

items.title: Gold Humanism Honor Society Chapter Grants 2026
items.description: GHHS chapter grants support chapter growth, innovation, and collaboration. The 2026 application window is 16 September – 30 October 2026.
items.eligibility: Gold Humanism Honor Society chapters

items.title: ASME PhD / Doctoral Grants
items.organization: Association for the Study of Medical Education
items.description: Doctoral studentship support (stipend plus consumables) and Annual Scholarship Meeting registration to present the work. Intended for applicants without a PhD who will undertake health professions education research.
items.eligibility: Those without PhDs, aligned with ASME doctoral funding rules
items.amount: Studentship stipend plus consumables and ASM registration

items.title: NBME Emerging Innovators Grants 2026
items.description: Supports early- and mid-career faculty, researchers, and program leaders. 2026 theme: Promoting Equitable and Innovative Assessment in Medical Education. Up to four awards of up to $25,000 for 1–2 year projects. Cycle closed 15 June 2026.
items.eligibility: PIs at LCME- or AOA/COCA-accredited medical schools or GME training facilities

items.title: NBME Stemmler Grants — 2027 cycle
items.description: Edward J. Stemmler, M.D. Medical Education Research Grant Program for mid- and senior-career researchers developing innovative assessment methodologies. Up to three awards of up to $150,000. Letters of intent for the 2027 cycle were due 29 June 2026; invited full proposals follow in early 2027.
items.eligibility: PIs with appointments at LCME- or AOA/COCA-accredited medical schools

items.title: Macy Foundation RFA — Ensuring Fairness in Clinical Assessment
items.description: Three two-year demonstration projects in medicine or nursing education to design, implement, and evaluate strategies for fairer clinical assessment, aligned with the 2022 Macy Conference recommendations. Letters of intent were due 30 March 2026; invited full applications 17 July 2026. Awards announced after the 21 October 2026 board meeting. Project period 1 November 2026 – 31 October 2028.
items.eligibility: Schools of medicine and nursing

items.title: Intealth 2026 Well-being Grant (IMG physicians in U.S. GME)
items.description: Funding for projects supporting international medical graduate physician well-being in U.S. graduate medical education. Faculty-led proposals must include an IMG resident mentee or collaborator. Deadline extended to 14 September 2026 and is now closed.
items.eligibility: IMG residents or faculty at U.S. GME programs that include IMG residents

items.title: ASME Small Grants
items.organization: Association for the Study of Medical Education
items.description: Research funding of up to £5,000 per project for individual ASME members. First-time applicants for research funding are welcome. The 2026 round closed 12 May 2026; ASME lists the next round as opening soon.
items.eligibility: Individual ASME members

items.title: AERA–NSF Research Grant
items.organization: American Educational Research Association (with National Science Foundation)
items.description: Research grants for faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and other doctoral-level scholars using rigorous quantitative methods on large-scale education data (NCES, NSF, SLDS, and other federal or health-related databases that can advance knowledge about education and learning). Awards are up to USD 25,000 for one-year projects or USD 35,000 for two-year projects; institutions may not charge overhead. The 2026 cycle closed 20 May 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PT. Medical and other health professions educators may apply when the project analyzes eligible large-scale data on education or learning.
items.deadlineNote: 11:59 p.m. PT. The 2026 cycle is closed.
items.amount: Up to USD 25,000 (1 year) or USD 35,000 (2 years)
items.eligibility: Faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and other doctoral-level scholars; U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, or non-U.S. citizens affiliated with a U.S. institution; prior AERA Research Grant recipients (as PI or Co-PI) are not eligible

items.title: AERA–NSF Dissertation Grant
items.organization: American Educational Research Association (with National Science Foundation)
items.description: One-year, non-renewable support for advanced doctoral students writing a dissertation that uses large-scale education data and quantitative methods. Award includes a stipend of up to USD 27,500, travel to an AERA research conference in Washington, DC, and a capstone institute at the AERA Annual Meeting. Health-related databases that can advance knowledge about education and learning are eligible. The 2026 cycle closed 20 May 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PT.
items.deadlineNote: 11:59 p.m. PT. The 2026 cycle is closed.
items.amount: Up to USD 27,500 stipend plus conference travel
items.eligibility: Advanced doctoral students at the dissertation-writing stage; U.S. citizens or permanent residents enrolled in a doctoral program, or non-U.S. citizens enrolled in a doctoral program at a U.S. institution

items.title: AERA Annual Meeting Graduate Student Assistance Fund (2027)
items.description: Need-based support for AERA graduate student members to offset the cost of attending the Annual Meeting. AERA makes up to 100 awards of a maximum of USD 500 each year. Students at institutions inside and outside the United States are eligible. Recipients of other AERA division or SIG travel funding for the same meeting are not eligible. AERA states that information for the 2027 Toronto meeting fund will be posted soon.
items.deadlineNote: 2027 call not yet posted. Watch the AMGSAF page.
items.eligibility: AERA graduate student members with demonstrated need; not already receiving other AERA travel funding for the same Annual Meeting
items.sourceName: AERA Annual Meeting Graduate Student Assistance Fund

items.title: Eastern Africa FAIMER Regional Institute — 2027 Fellowship
items.description: Two-year, part-time online fellowship in education methods, leadership, scholarship, and project evaluation for health professions faculty in East Africa. 2026 applications are closed. Applications for the 2027 program open in February 2027.
items.deadlineNote: Applications open February 2027; exact close date TBA
items.eligibility: Health professions faculty in East Africa (and other African regions considered)

items.title: Picker Gold Challenge Grants for Residency Training
items.description: 18-month grants of $15,000–$25,000 for GME interventions that put patient-centered care at the center of residency education, with a required institutional match. The 2023–2025 window is closed; watch the Gold Foundation page for the next cycle.
items.eligibility: GME programs; letter of support from department chair or DIO

items.title: The Clinical Teacher “New Voices in Health Professions Education” Award
items.organization: Association for the Study of Medical Education
items.description: Career-development award for early-career health professions educators and researchers seeking skills in peer review and writing papers. Open for submissions; closes 1 October 2026.
items.eligibility: Early-career HPE educators and researchers

items.title: JASME Group Innovation Prize
items.description: For a group of medical students and/or Foundation doctors who have developed an innovative project in medical education. £300, a certificate, and complimentary registration for one team member to the JASME conference.
items.amount: £300 plus JASME conference registration for one team member
items.eligibility: Medical students and/or Foundation doctors (group)

items.title: JASME Individual Innovation Prize
items.description: For medical students and Foundation-year doctors who have started a project. £300 in each category, a certificate, and complimentary registration for one winner per category at the next JASME conference.
items.eligibility: Medical students and Foundation-year doctors

items.title: ASME Gold Medal
items.organization: Association for the Study of Medical Education
items.description: For highly experienced scholars. Lifetime ASME membership and ASM plenary speaker slot, including registration and travel expenses.
items.eligibility: Highly experienced scholars

items.title: ASME President’s Medal
items.organization: Association for the Study of Medical Education
items.description: For highly experienced scholars, leaders, managers and/or policy makers. President’s medal and lifetime ASME membership. Listed as open for submissions.
items.eligibility: Highly experienced scholars, leaders, managers, policy makers

items.title: Mindfulness in Medical Education Research Award
items.description: For undergraduate students, postgraduate students/trainees, and healthcare professionals undertaking research related to mindfulness and wellbeing in medical education. £1,000 plus opportunities to present at ASME/MiME events.

items.title: IAMSE 2027 Travel Awards
items.organization: International Association of Medical Science Educators
items.description: Travel awards for junior faculty and students to attend the IAMSE Annual Conference. Faculty awards are up to $1,500 toward registration, lodging, and airfare. Applications due 15 December 2026; notifications in March 2027.
items.eligibility: Junior faculty and students; typically with an accepted presentation

items.title: ASME ASM Communication Prize
items.organization: Association for the Study of Medical Education
items.description: For ASME individual members presenting at the Annual Scholarship Meeting. Winner receives a copy of an ASME textbook and a certificate.
items.eligibility: ASME individual members

items.title: AAMC Award for Excellence in Medical Education
items.description: AAMC’s most prestigious medical education honor (formerly the Abraham Flexner Award). $10,000 prize. Nominations are open: anyone may nominate an individual or a team of two. Nominators of up to three finalists are invited to submit letters of support by 5 March 2027; those letters are due 2 April 2027. Winner notification by 30 July 2027.
items.eligibility: Faculty appointment at AAMC-member medical schools or health systems; individual or team of two

items.title: AMEE ASPIRE Awards 2026
items.description: Institutional excellence awards in nine categories, including assessment, curriculum, faculty development, simulation, social accountability, student engagement, and technology-enhanced learning. 2026 applications closed 28 February 2026.
items.eligibility: Health professions education institutions; application fee applies

items.title: Psychiatric education and its challenges
items.description: Collection on barriers and innovations in psychiatry training: stigma, curricula, clinical exposure, and regional resource disparities. Original research invited.

items.title: Disability in medical education
items.description: Collection on how medical curricula can address gaps in knowledge, skills, and attitudes related to disability in patients and in the profession.

items.title: Gamification and virtual reality in medical education — Part II
items.description: Follow-on collection on digital teaching, gamification, and VR in medical and related healthcare professions education.

items.title: Nutrition science in health professions education
items.description: Collection, in collaboration with the Global Nutrition Observatory for Medical Nutrition Education (GNOME), on nutrition science in health professions curricula.

items.title: Medical education for LGBTQ+ health
items.description: Collection on preparing learners for the unique health needs of LGBTQ+ patients and on related curriculum, assessment, and faculty development.

items.title: Health professions competency-based education innovations around the world
items.description: International collection on implementing and evaluating competency-based education innovations across health professions.

items.title: Disaster preparedness in medical education
items.description: Collection on educating health professionals to respond to natural and man-made disasters.

items.title: Health communication in medical education
items.description: Collection on teaching health communication to bridge literacy gaps, empower patients, and support collaborative relationships with communities.

items.title: Programmatic assessment
items.description: Collection on programmatic assessment as a structured approach to evaluating learner competencies across health professions education.

items.title: Advances in Medical Education
items.description: Special issue on transformative and inclusive pedagogies, high-tech instructional tools, equity, and the human-centric values of medical education. Research, reviews, and short communications invited.

items.title: Medicine, Meaning and Metaphor: Arts and Humanities as essential partners in medical and healthcare training
items.organization: Medical Humanities (BMJ) / Association for Medical Humanities
items.description: Topic collection on arts and humanities methods in clinical training: meaning in clinical encounters, embodiment, illness, culture, and community. Argues for further arts and humanities teaching in medical schools and postgraduate education.

items.title: IMSH 2027 — International Meeting on Simulation in Healthcare
items.description: Flagship annual meeting of SSH for how simulation is taught, practiced, researched, and used in patient safety and healthcare training. Formats include workshops, immersive courses, research abstracts, SimVentor innovations, and panels. The 2027 Call for Content closed 27 May 2026.

items.title: SESAM Annual Meeting 2026 — Lyon
items.description: 31st SESAM Annual Meeting, Europe’s main gathering for healthcare simulation education, research, and patient safety. Pre-congress 15–16 June; scientific meeting 17–19 June 2026. SESAM reported that abstract submissions had closed and were under review.

items.title: SESAM Annual Meeting 2027 — Riga
items.description: 32nd SESAM Annual Meeting. Pre-congress 15 June; scientific sessions 16–18 June 2027 at ATTA Center, Riga. Registration opens September 2026. The call for abstracts has not yet been posted.

items.title: INACSL27 — Call for Abstracts
items.organization: International Nursing Association for Clinical Simulation and Learning
items.description: Annual conference for simulationists, researchers, and educators in clinical simulation and learning. Submission types include teaching and learning projects, research, how-to sessions, workshops, lightning talks, and posters. Portal opened 15 September 2026. Accepted abstracts present in person.
items.deadlineNote: 11:59 p.m. CST

items.title: IPSSW 2027 — Call for Abstracts
items.description: International pediatric simulation meeting, themed “Learning, Leadership, Legacy: From Simulation to Sustainable Impact.” Abstracts invited from all aspects of pediatric simulation that show how learning, leadership, and innovation contribute to lasting impact on pediatric healthcare.

items.title: ASPiH 2026 — Simulation: The Next Era
items.organization: Association for Simulated Practice in Healthcare
items.description: UK/Europe simulation education conference at Harrogate Convention Centre. Pre-conference workshops 25 November; main conference and exhibition 26–27 November 2026. Abstracts closed 28 April 2026 (midnight GMT). Theme examines simulation as a driver of education, system learning, and healthcare transformation.
items.deadlineNote: midnight GMT

items.title: The Generalists in Medical Education 2026 — New Teams for New Times
items.description: Annual TGME conference for health professions educators and students, themed “New Teams for New Times: Collective Wisdom in Medical Education.” Interactive formats include round tables, descriptive sessions, ignite talks, panels, problem-solving and skill-acquisition sessions, plus traditional and “Blue Sky” posters. Call for proposals closed 17 May 2026. Registration includes sessions, meals, a reception, and (except student registrations) a subscription to Teaching and Learning in Medicine. Often held adjacent to AAMC Learn Serve Lead; 2026 is in Anaheim the same week.
items.deadlineNote: 11:59 p.m. EST
items.location: Anaheim Marriott Suites, Anaheim, California, USA

items.title: AERA 2027 Annual Meeting — Division I (Education in the Professions)
items.organization: American Educational Research Association — Division I
items.description: AERA’s 2027 Annual Meeting will be held in Toronto, 14–18 April 2027, under the theme “Transcending Borders and Boundaries in Education Research: Toward a Beloved Global Community.” Division I (Education in the Professions) is the AERA home for research on education in professional practice, including the health professions, from higher education through lifelong learning and assessment. The 2027 call for submissions closed 24 July 2026. Watch the Annual Meeting page for registration and housing.
